findings.title: JWT Token Verification Bypassed via jwt.decode()
findings.impact: An attacker can forge JWT tokens and impersonate any user, including those with elevated privileges. The jwt.decode() function decodes without signature verification.
findings.evidence: Line 4: 'const claims = jwt.decode(bearer);' does not pass a secret parameter. Line 10 has the same issue. The function should use jwt.verify(token, secret) instead.
findings.recommendation: Replace all jwt.decode() calls with jwt.verify(bearer, process.env.JWT_SECRET || 'your-secret-key'). This enforces signature verification on every token claim extraction.

findings.title: SQL Injection in /invoices Endpoint via order Parameter
findings.impact: An attacker can execute arbitrary SQL queries by manipulating the 'order' query parameter, allowing database exfiltration, modification, or deletion.
findings.evidence: Line 20: 'const order = req.query.order || \'created_at\'; ... ORDER BY ${order}' - the order parameter is directly interpolated into the SQL query without any sanitization or parameterization.
findings.recommendation: Use a whitelist-based approach similar to the SORTABLE map in the /payments endpoint. Define allowed column names and validate the order parameter against this list before interpolation.

findings.title: Authorization Bypass: Any Authenticated User Can Access Any Invoice
findings.impact: An authenticated attacker can retrieve invoices belonging to other users by manipulating the invoice ID parameter.
findings.evidence: Line 12-14: The /invoices/:id endpoint queries 'SELECT * FROM invoices WHERE id = $1' without checking the owner_id field. The /receipts/:id endpoint (line 18-22) correctly includes 'AND owner_id = $2' check, but the invoice endpoint omits this.
findings.recommendation: Add the owner_id check: 'WHERE id = $1 AND owner_id = $2' with [req.params.id, req.user.id] as parameters. Also ensure req.user is populated from authentication middleware.

findings.title: SSRF Vulnerability in Logo Fetching via Unvalidated Redirects
findings.impact: An attacker can trick the server into making requests to internal services (localhost, private IPs, cloud metadata endpoints) by providing a URL that redirects to those targets.
findings.evidence: Line 5: 'async function fetchLogo(url) { const response = await fetch(url, { redirect: \'follow\' });' - the redirect option is set to \'follow\', allowing the server to follow redirects to arbitrary hosts. The URL is taken directly from req.body.logoUrl without hostname validation.
findings.recommendation: Implement hostname validation using URL parsing (e.g., check that parsed.hostname is in an allowed list). Set redirect to \'error\' to reject any redirect responses. Optionally add request timeout and size limits.

findings.title: XSS Vulnerability in Invoice Note Rendering
findings.impact: User-supplied invoice notes can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript into the rendered invoice, leading to session hijacking, credential theft, or malware distribution.
findings.evidence:
Line 4: 'function invoiceNote(note) { return `
${note}
`; }' - the note parameter is directly interpolated without escaping. While escapeHtml is imported and used in customerName(), it is NOT used for invoiceNote().
findings.recommendation:
Use escapeHtml() consistently: return `
${escapeHtml(note)}
;`. Audit all user-supplied data that flows into HTML rendering and apply escaping.

findings.title: Missing Authentication on /branding/preview Endpoint
findings.impact: An unauthenticated attacker can access the /branding/preview endpoint, triggering logo fetches on demand. This can be used to probe internal services or amplify SSRF attacks.
findings.evidence: Line 46: 'router.post(\'/branding/preview\', async (req, res) => { const image = await fetchLogo(req.body.logoUrl);' - no middleware or authentication check is present before this handler. The endpoint accepts any request.
findings.recommendation: Add authentication middleware (e.g., router.post(\'/branding/preview\', authMiddleware, ...)) to ensure only authenticated users can trigger logo fetches. Verify req.user is populated.

findings.title: Incomplete SQL Injection Mitigation in /payments Endpoint
findings.impact: Although the /payments endpoint uses a whitelist (SORTABLE), the pattern could be bypassed by edge cases or column injection if the whitelist is extended improperly.
findings.evidence: Line 38-42: The endpoint uses a whitelist-based approach (SORTABLE[req.query.sort] || SORTABLE.date), which is better than /invoices but still interpolates into the SQL query. If new columns are added to SORTABLE carelessly, the pattern could re-introduce SQL injection.
findings.recommendation: Continue using the whitelist approach but add strict validation. Use parameterized queries or an ORM to avoid string interpolation entirely. Document the whitelist as a security-critical component and enforce code review for changes.
